blocks.x: Agentic S&OP execution — planner hours down 50% and on-time-in-full up 6 points through the peak season
a packaging producer whose planners spent Mondays rebuilding spreadsheets that ERP already knew the answers to. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline month measured the Mondays: 22 planner hours per week on data assembly, 87.4% OTIF, and the peak-season plan agreed in week nine of a ten-week run-up.
Constraints — machine windows, changeover costs, minimum runs — lived in planners' heads and three spreadsheets. The ERP plan was theoretically optimal and practically ignored.

We moved S&OP execution to governed agents: demand, inventory and constraint data assembled automatically into the planning model, scenario options generated with each constraint's cost visible, planners choosing between scenarios instead of building them, and execution deviations feeding back weekly. The Monday meeting now starts at the decision, not the spreadsheet.
